steps.text: Arrange leaves around the centre, pointing inward or outward. Repeat a colour or alternate two shapes all the way around. Leave gaps if you like; the circle does not need to be perfect.
steps.youngTask: Try an alternating red-yellow or broad-narrow pattern.

steps.title: Grow a new pattern each ring
steps.text: Add an outer ring with a different repeated pattern: twig, stone, twig, stone, or leaves between pinecones. Build another loop if there is room. Use the materials you have, and stop at any size.
steps.littleTask: Place a leaf or stone in each gap.
steps.youngTask: Change the repeating rule for each new ring.

steps.title: Give it your own character
steps.text: Look at the whole design. Make the leaves look like sun rays, soft petals or fierce spikes, or keep a calm repeating pattern. Change any pieces you want and take a picture of your finished mandala.
steps.littleTask: Choose whether it feels cute, fierce or beautiful.
steps.youngTask: Adjust spacing, add a final border, and explain your pattern.
steps.adultTask: Photograph the design, then help restore the space without disturbing living things.

keep: This is temporary outdoor art. Take a picture before wind or weather changes the pattern.
cleanup: Clear paths and play areas when finished. Return loose natural materials only where permitted and leave living plants and small habitats as you found them.
extension: Make a tiny mandala beside a larger one, try only two colours, or let a different person design each new ring.
examples: A woodland ring of cones and stones
reviewStatus: Draft guide — not yet physically tested or reviewed.

title: Meet your fall friends
subtitle: Leaf dresses, twig arms and a little woodland personality.
description: Make leaf fairies and woodland characters with twig limbs, leafy clothes and expressive faces. Keep them loose on the ground or make a flat picture on card. Extra cutting and tiny details are optional.

materials.name: Fallen leaves for clothes, hair and wings
Smooth, blunt fallen twigs for a body and limbs
Flat ground, a reusable tray or card backing
Paper face circle prepared by a grown-up and a crayon
Child-safe scissors for optional leaf or paper details
Child-safe water-based craft glue, chosen by a grown-up
materials.quantity: A few small dabs for card only

materials.name: Clean soil and a little water for optional temporary mud paste
Small reusable bowl and spoon if mixing mud

adultNote: Supervise scissors and prepare small paper shapes if needed. Use naturally shaped leaves for a no-cut version. A grown-up chooses any glue; keep it on card and take the artwork indoors. Mud can hold some flat pieces briefly but will not make a strong upright puppet.
youngRole: Design the character, layer leaf clothes and add a face, wings or a leafy hairstyle.

steps.title: Choose who you will meet
steps.text: Spread your leaves and twigs on a tray beside a flat work space. Imagine a fairy, forest explorer or funny leaf person. Choose broad leaves for clothes and smaller leaves for hair or wings.
steps.youngTask: Pick colours and shapes that match your character.
steps.adultTask: Check materials and prepare a paper face circle if wanted.

steps.title: Lay out the body and face
steps.text: Lay a short twig flat for the body. Add twig arms and legs around it. Place a paper circle or small leaf above the body for the face. Try a waving pose or a dancing pose before adding clothes.
steps.youngTask: Arrange the limbs and head so the character is easy to recognise.
steps.adultTask: Help keep twig ends blunt and all pieces lying flat.

steps.title: Dress your fall friend
steps.text: Overlap leaves over the body to make a dress, coat or tunic. Add leaf wings, a hat or colourful hair. Use each leaf’s natural shape, or ask a grown-up before making small cuts with child-safe scissors.
steps.youngTask: Layer leaves from the bottom up and try different costumes.
steps.adultTask: Supervise any cutting; offer the no-cut version as an equally good choice.

steps.title: Add details your way
steps.text: Draw a face on the paper or place leaf features. Leave the friend loose, or use a tiny dab of mud under flat pieces. For a card picture, a grown-up may help with approved glue. Keep it flat while it sets.
steps.youngTask: Add an expression and choose whether to keep the pieces loose.
steps.adultTask: Mud is temporary. Use glue only on backing and follow its drying instructions; do not promise a standing puppet.

steps.title: Introduce your fall friends
steps.text: Give each friend a name and a story. Arrange a little scene on the ground or beside your fairy garden. Photograph the finished friends. Your colours, clothes and characters can look completely different from the examples.
steps.youngTask: Create a companion or tell a story about your character.
steps.adultTask: Bring paper and glued artwork indoors after play, and help tidy the work space.

keep: Keep the characters flat. Photograph loose or mud-held friends; display a glued card picture indoors once it has dried.
cleanup: Take all paper and glued materials home. Reuse tools and trays, clear the play space and wash hands after using soil.
extension: Make friends with different moods, add a leafy pet, or introduce your characters to the Fall Fairy Garden.
waitLabel: Optional glue: follow its drying instructions. Mud holds only temporarily.
reviewStatus: Draft guide — not yet physically tested or reviewed.

title: Make a little snowman
subtitle: A small snowy friend with a big smile.
description: Pack three small snowballs, stack them low and add a pressed face with removable twig arms.

materials.name: Clean packable snow
Smooth short twigs for arms and optional face details
Blunt twig for pressing features
Warm clothing and waterproof mittens

adultNote: An adult checks the weather, clothing and safe location away from roads, water, roof edges and falling ice. Keep the snowman about 30 cm tall and stop for warm-up breaks.
littleRole: Pack the base and press the face with adult help.
youngRole: Shape and stack smaller sections, then check balance.
togetherPlan: Younger makers pack the broad base; older makers shape the upper sections. Add the face and name your friend together.

steps.title: Test a handful of snow
steps.text: With mittens on, squeeze a small handful. If it holds together, use that snow. If it remains powdery, switch to a flat snow picture rather than adding hot water or salt.
steps.youngTask: Check whether the ball holds.
steps.adultTask: Choose a safe area and check conditions.

steps.title: Pack a broad base
steps.text: Pack a snow mound about 15 cm wide on flat ground. Round the sides with mittened hands and flatten the top slightly. Keep the base broad and low.
steps.youngTask: Shape a stable base.
steps.adultTask: Help pack the mound as needed.

steps.title: Add two smaller balls
steps.text: Make a middle ball about 10 cm wide and a head about 7 cm wide. An adult helps set them on the base. Press a little snow into the joins so the stack stays still.
steps.youngTask: Shape the middle and head.
steps.adultTask: Lift and steady the sections.

steps.title: Press a face and add arms
steps.text: Use the blunt twig to press shallow eyes and a smile. An adult may instead place a few short, blunt twigs lightly in the surface for a nose or mouth. Press two short twigs gently into the sides for arms. Keep the face simple and every piece removable.
steps.youngTask: Place the arms evenly.
steps.adultTask: Check twig ends and place any facial pieces.

steps.title: Meet your snowy friend
steps.text: Give the snowman a name and look at it from different sides. Collect the tool and remove every twig from the face and arms when finished. Leave only clean snow and take a warm-up break.
steps.youngTask: Tell a snowy story.
steps.adultTask: Check comfort, collect materials and return indoors when needed.

keep: Enjoy the changing snow shape where permitted; it will melt.
cleanup: Remove all twigs, tools and other added pieces before leaving.
extension: Try a squat two-section friend with the same method.
reviewStatus: Draft guide — not yet physically tested or reviewed.

title: A pocket-sized snow village
subtitle: A whole winter world, made small.
description: Mould little snow houses with reusable cups, connect them with paths and invent the residents. No tunnels or climbable structures.

materials.name: Clean packable snow
Reusable cups or small tubs, under 15 cm tall
Smooth blunt twig for marking
Warm clothing and waterproof mittens

adultNote: An adult chooses a safe snow area and supervises weather breaks. Keep structures miniature and solid; no digging tunnels, hollow shelters or roofs people could enter.
youngRole: Mould low houses and design a village layout.

steps.title: Plan a small neighbourhood
steps.text: On flat snow, mark a patch about 50 cm across with the blunt twig. Draw where two houses and a path will go. Leave space to walk around the village.
steps.youngTask: Sketch a simple layout in the snow.
steps.adultTask: Check the area and clothing.

steps.title: Pack the first mould
steps.text: Fill a cup with packable snow, pressing each small handful down with a mitten. Level the top. If the snow will not pack, use a flat relief picture instead.
steps.youngTask: Pack the cup without leaving large gaps.
steps.adultTask: Help test the snow.

steps.title: Turn out two houses
steps.text: Turn the cup upside down onto the planned spot. Tap gently and lift it straight up. Make a second house with the other cup. Keep both solid and low.
steps.youngTask: Lift the mould slowly and compare the shapes.
steps.adultTask: Help release a stuck mould without forcing it.

steps.title: Connect the village
steps.text: Use the blunt twig to trace a shallow path between houses. Press a door and window shape onto each surface without hollowing out the buildings. Add a small snow courtyard if you like.
steps.youngTask: Draw connected paths and shallow details.
steps.adultTask: Keep the markings shallow and structures solid.

steps.title: Tell the winter story
steps.text: Give the village a name and invent its residents. Gather the cups and twig, check the area for anything left behind, and take a warm-up break.
steps.youngTask: Tell a story that visits both houses.
steps.adultTask: Check everyone is comfortable and collect equipment.

keep: Leave only snow where permitted and expect it to change with the weather.
cleanup: Retrieve every tool and added material.
extension: Arrange three low moulded houses around a round courtyard.
reviewStatus: Draft guide — not yet physically tested or reviewed.

title: Pictures in the snow
subtitle: Turn a snowy patch into a little canvas.
description: Make a flat snow picture by drawing an outline, adding low shapes and pressing patterns into the surface.

materials.name: Clean packable snow
materials.quantity: A safe patch about 40 cm wide

materials.name: Smooth blunt twig
Warm clothing and waterproof mittens

adultNote: An adult checks the location and weather and stays close. Keep the picture flat and low, with no digging, tunnels or tall structures.
littleRole: Shape a simple snowy face, flower or animal.

steps.title: Smooth a snow canvas
steps.text: Choose a flat patch about 40 cm wide. Pat the surface with mittened hands until it is gently even. Leave the snow on the ground rather than digging a hole.
steps.adultTask: Choose a safe area and check clothing.

steps.title: Draw a broad outline
steps.text: Use the blunt twig to draw a large circle, flower or animal head. Keep the outline simple enough to follow with one finger.
steps.adultTask: Guide the outline if needed.

steps.title: Add low raised shapes
steps.text: Place small handfuls of snow inside the outline. Press them into shallow mounds no more than about 3 cm high. Add round cheeks, petals or two broad ears.
steps.adultTask: Help pack pieces that crumble.

steps.title: Press a pattern
steps.text: Use the twig tip or a mitten edge to press shallow dots and lines. Add eyes and a smile, petal lines or a fur pattern without making deep holes.
steps.adultTask: Supervise the blunt tool.

steps.title: Give the picture a name
steps.text: Stand beside the picture and look down at the shapes and shadows. Name it, collect the twig and take a warm-up break. Leave only snow behind.
steps.adultTask: Check comfort and gather the tool.

keep: The picture changes with light, weather and melting; save a photo or drawing if desired.
cleanup: Take the twig and all equipment home.
extension: Try a simple animal face with two broad ears.
reviewStatus: Draft guide — not yet physically tested or reviewed.

title: Winter twig stars
subtitle: A little woodland sparkle, without the glitter.
description: Arrange five similar twigs in a star, then secure the five outer points with short string ties. Make and display it indoors.

materials.name: Smooth straight dry twigs, about 18 cm long
Cotton string, pre-cut
Paper for a star guide
Small paper snowflake, optional

adultNote: An adult prepares twigs, ties or checks the joins and trims loose string. Display flat; do not wear it or leave string decorations outdoors.
youngRole: Follow the star layout and help wrap each join.

steps.title: Make a five-point guide
steps.text: Draw five dots around a circle on paper: one at the top, two at the sides and two lower down. Number them around the circle 1 to 5. Join 1 to 3 to 5 to 2 to 4 to 1.
steps.youngTask: Draw the star guide.
steps.adultTask: Prepare smooth twigs of similar length.

steps.title: Lay the five twigs
steps.text: Lay a twig along each line of the guide. Let twig ends overlap by about 2 cm at each outer point. Keep the star flat and adjust until the points are even.
steps.youngTask: Match the five twigs to the guide.
steps.adultTask: Help keep the overlapping twigs in place.

steps.title: Tie the first two points
steps.text: At one outer point, wrap a short string around the two overlapping twig ends three times, then tie a double knot. Repeat at the next point while an adult holds the star flat.
steps.youngTask: Wrap each crossing neatly.
steps.adultTask: Tie or check the knots and hold the layout.

steps.title: Secure the remaining points
steps.text: Tie the remaining three outer points the same way. Gently lift one edge to check the shape holds. Tighten a loose join, then have an adult trim long string tails.
steps.youngTask: Check the five joins.
steps.adultTask: Finish knots and trim string tails.

steps.title: Display your winter star
steps.text: Remove the paper guide and lay the star on a shelf. Tuck a small paper snowflake under a tie if desired. Keep it away from heat, flames and younger children.
steps.youngTask: Choose a simple display spot.
steps.adultTask: Check the star and display location.

keep: Keep dry indoors and inspect knots before moving.
cleanup: Untie string for reuse and sort untreated twigs separately.
extension: Make a second star of the same size and place them side by side.
reviewStatus: Draft guide — not yet physically tested or reviewed.

title: A snowy pinecone forest
subtitle: A cosy winter world for the kitchen table.
description: Stand pinecones in reusable clay, dab a little white paint onto the scales and arrange them into a tiny winter forest.

materials.name: Dry pinecones checked by an adult
Reusable modelling clay
Washable white poster paint
Small sponge or brush
Card or reusable tray, about 25 × 30 cm

adultNote: An adult checks cone scales and the paint label. Protect the table and wash hands afterward. Painted cones must not be returned to natural habitats.
littleRole: Press clay bases and dab snowy tips with help.
youngRole: Arrange the forest and apply a light snow pattern.
togetherPlan: Younger makers prepare the bases; older makers arrange and paint the trees. Plan a winding path together.

steps.title: Prepare three tree bases
steps.text: Flatten each piece of clay into a small disc on the tray. Space the three discs apart, leaving a clear path between them. Keep unused paint closed.
steps.youngTask: Plan where the path will pass.
steps.adultTask: Check the cones and protect the workspace.

steps.title: Stand the pinecone trees
steps.text: Press the wide end of each cone into a clay disc. Keep the cones upright and low. If one leans, widen its clay base and press it in a little more.
steps.youngTask: Check the balance of each tree.
steps.adultTask: Help press pointed or awkward cones safely.

steps.title: Make a light snow dab
steps.text: Put one teaspoon of paint on a scrap of card. Touch the sponge to the paint, then dab once on the scrap so it is not dripping.
steps.youngTask: Control how much paint is on the sponge.
steps.adultTask: Read the paint label and help prepare the small amount.

steps.title: Add snowy tips
steps.text: Dab a little white paint on the outer tips of the cone scales. Leave brown spaces between dabs so the cone still shows. Turn the tray rather than holding the wet cone.
steps.youngTask: Keep the snow pattern light and even.
steps.adultTask: Help reach awkward areas without touching sharp scales.

steps.title: Let the forest dry
steps.text: Leave the tray flat until the paint is dry, following its label. Trace an imaginary path between the trees and name the forest. Wash the sponge and everyone’s hands.
steps.youngTask: Tell a story along the path.
steps.adultTask: Manage paint cleanup and check drying before handling.

keep: Keep indoors and dry. Paint drying time depends on the product and amount used.
cleanup: Remove clay for reuse where clean. Dispose of painted cones as craft waste according to local rules; never return them outdoors.
extension: Add a paper animal beside the trees after the paint dries.
reviewStatus: Draft guide — not yet physically tested or reviewed.
waitLabel: Allow paint to dry fully before moving; follow the paint label.

title: Make a little snow man
subtitle: A handful of snow, a twiggy smile and a new winter friend.
description: Build a snow person with its own character: a lumpy friend with a pine-cone hat, a classic carrot-nose snowman, or a funny upside-down one with boots. Start small, shape two or three snowballs, and make its face and pose your own.
setting: Outside on a flat snowy patch

materials.name: Clean snow that packs when squeezed
Short blunt fallen twigs
Smooth stones suitable for the children
Fallen leaf or small pine cone
Carrot for a nose
Scarf and small boots for an upside-down variation
Warm outdoor clothes and waterproof mittens

adultNote: Choose a flat patch away from roads, water and overhead snow or ice. Check loose materials and choose stone sizes suitable for the children. Keep the snow person small and low, with no heavy lifting. Take warm-up breaks and stop if anyone feels cold or wet.
littleRole: Pat the snowballs and choose the face and twig arms.
youngRole: Help flatten the joining surfaces and give the snow person its own character.
togetherPlan: A Little Maker shapes the base and picks the face. A Young Creator helps join the smaller snowball and add details. Work side by side and let the youngest maker choose the smile.

steps.title: Find snow that sticks together
steps.text: Dress warmly and choose a flat snowy patch with a grown-up. Squeeze a handful of clean snow in your mittens. If it holds together, you are ready. If it stays powdery, save this build for stickier snow rather than adding water that may freeze.
steps.youngTask: Check whether the snow holds its shape.
steps.adultTask: Approve the place and check everyone is warm and dry.

steps.title: Pat a sturdy little base
steps.text: Press several handfuls into one round snowball. Set it on the ground and flatten the bottom so it sits steadily. Keep it small enough to shape with your hands; this friend does not need giant rolled snowballs.
steps.youngTask: Flatten the bottom and check it sits steadily.

steps.title: Add a smaller snowball
steps.text: Make a smaller ball for the head. Flatten the top of the base a little, set the head on it and gently press loose snow around the join. You can add a small middle ball first for a three-ball friend. Keep the whole stack low and steady.
steps.youngTask: Help flatten and join the snowballs.
steps.adultTask: Help with joining if the snowballs wobble; make them smaller if needed.

steps.title: Give your snow person a face
steps.text: Gently press suitable smooth stones into the head for eyes. Make a smile with a curved twig or marks in the snow and add two twig arms. Try a pine cone for a hat or a carrot for a nose. For an upside-down version, a grown-up can help put the face on the bottom ball and small boots on top of a low, stable stack.
steps.youngTask: Add arms and a hat or extra snow details.
steps.adultTask: Check twig ends and help with the upside-down variation; keep the stack low and steady.

steps.title: Meet your little snow man
steps.text: Name your new friend and take a picture. Give it a snowball neighbour, a pine-cone hat or a different expression. Try a traditional snowman or an upside-down joke with a grown-up helping. Make each friend different, then head inside for a warm-up break.
steps.littleTask: Choose a name and say hello.
steps.youngTask: Make a neighbour with a different expression.
steps.adultTask: Collect loose decorations when play is finished, before the snow melts.

keep: Snow changes with the weather. Enjoy your little friend outside during play and take a picture before it melts.
cleanup: Gather every stone, twig, carrot and extra decoration when finished. Take any scarf and boots indoors, leave the snowy patch clear and dry your mittens.
extension: Make a tiny family with different shapes and expressions, or give each snow person a name and a winter story.
examples: An upside-down snow man with boots
waitLabel: Snow needs to pack together. Warm-up breaks are part of making.
reviewStatus: Draft guide — not yet physically tested or reviewed.
natureNote: Use fallen or already-loose materials where collecting is allowed. Leave living plants and animals alone, and gather every decoration before the snow melts.

title: A pocket-sized snow village
subtitle: Twig-roof cottages, rounded snow houses or a tiny snow castle.
description: Build a miniature village from snow, rocks and twigs. Try a twig-roof cottage, rounded snow houses with sprigs on top and twig-lined paths, or a tiny block-shaped snow castle. Mix different shapes and make a little winter world of your own.
setting: Outside on a flat snowy patch

materials.name: Clean snow that packs when squeezed
Short blunt fallen twigs
Small manageable smooth stones
Small reusable cups or containers for shaping
Already-loose evergreen sprigs or dry stems
Warm outdoor clothes and waterproof mittens

adultNote: Choose a flat place away from roads, water and overhead snow or ice. Keep every cottage hand-sized, solid and low; these are models, not shelters to enter. Use small stones at ground level and short blunt twigs. Take warm-up breaks and stop if anyone feels cold or wet.
youngRole: Choose the house shapes, decorate their roofs and connect the village with paths.

steps.title: Plan a tiny winter village
steps.text: Dress warmly and find a flat snowy patch with a grown-up. Test that a handful of snow holds together. Set out a few stones and short blunt twigs, then mark places for two or three hand-sized houses with room for paths between them.
steps.youngTask: Choose where the cottages and paths will go.
steps.adultTask: Check the place, materials and weather; use snow that already packs together.

steps.title: Shape solid snowy cottages
steps.text: Pat snow into two or three small solid mounds. Shape a cottage with a peaked roof, round houses with flat tops, or low rectangular castle blocks. You can pack snow into a cup or container and turn it out first. Keep each base broad and the inside solid.
steps.youngTask: Try a peaked cottage, rounded house or block-shaped castle.

steps.title: Give each roof its character
steps.text: For a cottage, lay short twigs on the snowy roof slopes and dust them lightly with snow. For round houses, tuck an already-loose evergreen sprig or dry stem into each top. For a castle, shape low snow turrets. Let the solid snow support the details and keep rocks at ground level.
steps.youngTask: Choose twig slopes, sprig-topped roofs or little snow turrets.
steps.adultTask: Check roof pieces and keep all the miniature buildings low and solid.

steps.title: Add doors and village paths
steps.text: Press a shallow door shape into the front of each cottage without hollowing it out. Arrange a few stones at ground level around the doorway. Connect the houses with a finger-drawn path and use small stones or short twigs to mark its edges.
steps.youngTask: Make door outlines and connect the cottages with paths.

steps.title: Tell a snowy village story
steps.text: Look around your tiny village. Try one twig-roof cottage, a group of round sprig-topped houses, or a snow castle with a pebble courtyard. Connect their doors with branching paths. Imagine who lives there, photograph the scene and gather your decorations before warming up inside.
steps.youngTask: Give the cottages names and invent a village story.
steps.adultTask: Help collect all roof twigs and stones before leaving the making place.

keep: The village is temporary outdoor play. Photograph the twig roofs and winding paths before snow and weather change them.
cleanup: Gather all stones, twigs, sprigs, dry stems, containers and supplies. Leave the making place clear and bring outdoor clothes inside to dry.
extension: Add a tiny snowy meeting place, draw a new route through the village, or tell a story about a visitor arriving at the smallest cottage.
examples: Round snow houses with twig paths
waitLabel: Hand-sized solid models only. Keep rocks at ground level.
reviewStatus: Draft guide — not yet physically tested or reviewed.
natureNote: Use fallen or already-loose materials where collecting is allowed. Leave living plants and animals alone, and gather every decoration before the snow melts.

title: Snowy Friends
subtitle: Mice, rabbits, cats, a bear or a turtle: choose your snowy friend.
description: Turn snow into mice, rabbits, cats, a bear or a turtle. Try tiny creatures, a seated animal or a flat shape on the ground. Older makers can practise shaping and joining snow, then add ears, whiskers and faces to create a friend with its own personality.
setting: Outside on a flat snowy patch
difficulty: A step beyond a snow person

materials.name: Clean snow that packs when squeezed
Smooth stones for eyes and a nose
Short blunt twigs or loose dry grass
Small flat smooth pebbles for mouse ears; fallen leaves for cat ears
Small carrot or carrot pieces for noses
Warm outdoor clothes and waterproof mittens

adultNote: For older makers practising more detailed shaping. Choose a flat place away from roads, water and overhead snow or ice. Start with a low body and broad joins. A grown-up can help with taller ears or seated animals; no hidden sticks are needed inside the snow. Check natural pieces, take warm-up breaks and stop if anyone feels cold or wet.
youngRole: Plan the animal shape, blend the joins and add recognisable details.

steps.title: Choose a snowy creature
steps.text: Dress warmly and test a handful of snow with a grown-up. Choose mice, a rabbit, cat, bear, turtle or an invented creature. Think about its biggest shape first: an oval mouse, a seated animal or a low turtle shell. Snow that will not pack can wait for another day.
steps.youngTask: Choose one creature and picture its main body shape.
steps.adultTask: Check the place and materials, and make sure everyone stays warm and dry.

steps.title: Build one low body
steps.text: Press snow into a mound with a broad base. Smooth an oval mouse, a seated rabbit, cat or bear, or a wide dome for a turtle. Begin with a small body. A grown-up can help you build up a larger seated shape without lifting heavy snow.
steps.youngTask: Build and smooth the main body before adding small parts.

steps.title: Shape and join the small parts
steps.text: Pinch a mouse snout from the front, or join a head and paws to a seated animal. Give a turtle a head and four flat flippers. A cat can have a curved tail supported along its body. Press extra snow around each join and blend it in; shorten parts that keep falling off.
steps.youngTask: Add the head and limbs, then blend each join with loose snow.

steps.title: Add ears, a face and texture
steps.text: Shape long rabbit ears, pointed cat ears or round bear ears with broad bases and grown-up help. Mice can have small flat pebble ears, a carrot-tip nose and grass whiskers. Press each pebble partly into the snow so it stays steady. Fallen leaves can make pointed cat ears. Use stone eyes or shallow carved features. A blunt twig can mark a turtle shell or a cat face.
steps.youngTask: Add the details that make your creature recognisable.
steps.adultTask: Check twig ends and natural pieces; keep the snow sculpture low and stable.

steps.title: Introduce your snowy friend
steps.text: Look at your creature from a few sides and reshape any part you want. Name it, photograph it and try a small companion. Different-sized ears, a crooked smile or an uneven shell can make your friend special. Gather loose details and head inside for a warm-up break.
steps.youngTask: Name your creature and decide what makes it special.
steps.adultTask: Help collect all stones, leaves and twig details before leaving.

keep: Enjoy the sculpture outside during play. Take a picture to remember the details as the snow softens or melts.
cleanup: Collect stones, leaves, grass, twigs, carrot pieces and pebble ears from the sculpture. Leave the snowy patch clear and dry your mittens indoors.
extension: Make a whole snowy animal family, try both carved and pebble faces, or invent a creature by changing its body shape, ears or tail.

A rabbit and its little friend
A snow cat meets a tiny mouse
waitLabel: Broad joins and short details are easier to keep in place.
reviewStatus: Draft guide — not yet physically tested or reviewed.
natureNote: Use fallen or already-loose materials where collecting is allowed. Leave living plants and animals alone, and gather every decoration before the snow melts.
